Subject: Private deployment ops charter + control/data interface matrix

Team —

Per the on-prem deployment working session last week, attaching a first-pass ops charter and the control-vs-data interface matrix for the Acme private VPC. The goal here is to make the demarcation explicit so Security can sign off on egress controls and our SREs can prepare the runbook.

Key asks in this note:
- Review the interface matrix sheet and call out any missing RPCs/endpoints or observability routes.
- Confirm proposed CIDR split between control and data planes (sheet has a suggested /18 for tenant data, /22 for control-plane management).
- Validate KMS/HSM touchpoints and cert rotation flow in the runbook draft — we need to ensure no customer keys ever leave the HSM.

I've referenced two diagrams (segregation-diagram-v2.png) and the runbook draft. Plan to sync with Acme (Claire) on Thursday to validate their firewall tiers and NAT expectations.

Timeline: we need signoff from Security by 2029-05-20 to keep the staging cutover on-track.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Soojin — quick notes after skimming the matrix:

- Control plane endpoints: we should explicitly call out the management API (mgt.redwood.local:8443) and the certificate distribution service (cds.redwood.local). Add a column for 'consistent port expectations' (TCP/UDP) — some customers lock down UDP and that affects leader election/coordination.
- Egress: are we expecting per-tenant NAT or shared NAT per pod? The current sheet assumes shared NAT which affects logging and SNAT source IP / auditability. If Acme requires source IP preservation for their IDS, we'll need per-tenant NAT.
- BGP: if Acme prefers on-prem BGP adjacency to our edge, include the ASN and expected route filters in the matrix.

I'll add inline comments in the spreadsheet and flag open questions. For the runbook, I'll add an ops checklist for control-plane failover and KV cache rebuild steps.

-kim
Kimberly Park
Sr Manager, Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment ops charter + control/data interface matrix

Claire — forwarding our draft materials so your networking/security teams can validate the boundary assumptions before Thursday's sync.

Short context for your team: Redwood will run a private control plane cluster inside Acme's VPC; data-plane inference nodes will sit in tenant-dedicated subnets with strict egress rules. We propose:
- Control plane management traffic limited to the management subnet and a small set of IPs from Redwood's operations network.
- All telemetry metrics/trace traffic to be TLS-only to telemetry.redwood.com over port 443 (we will provide cert pinning details).
- Egress policy with a mandatory egress proxy if any external destinations are required from inference containers.

Can you please confirm Acme's preferred approach for NAT (shared vs per-tenant) and whether the on-prem firewall team needs explicit source IP ranges for service account calls?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Claire Park <claire.park@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: eng@nimbuscloud.com, network-ops@acme.com
Date: Wed, 15 May 2029 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment ops charter + control/data interface matrix

Thanks for the materials — Acme network/security here. A few clarifications:

- We need per-tenant NAT. Our IDS correlates traffic by source IP and we cannot consolidate customer traffic behind a shared SNAT.
- BGP adjacency: we are open to iBGP/EBGP but require sessions to hit an intermediate route-reflector; we will share the ASN and prefix filters during the call.
- KMS/HSM: on-prem HSM is mandatory for our PHI workloads; any calls to Redwood's KMS must be over a pinned mTLS connection and originate from a defined set of management IPs.
- Egress proxy: we prefer an explicit egress proxy (squid/mitm-transparent) in a dedicated service subnet so we can enforce content policies and TLS inspection.

We'll be on the call Thursday at 11:00 PT. I've attached our network constraints doc (see link in email).

- Claire Park
Senior Security Engineer, Acme Corp

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: All
Date: Wed, 15 May 2029 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment ops charter + control/data interface matrix — action items

Captured action items after Claire's responses and the spreadsheet comments:

1) Kimberly to update the matrix with explicit ports and per-tenant NAT flows; include a column for 'auditability impact' and 'IDS compatibility'.
2) Marissa to draft the BGP adjacency appendix (ASN / RR / filters) and coordinate with Acme network-ops during Thursday's call.
3) Aditya to update runbook-draft.md with HSM call flow, cert pinning steps, and a fallback for local key wrapping if HSM is unavailable.
4) Jordan to prototype the egress-proxy deployment pattern (dedicated subnet + autoscaling squid) and provide an initial helm chart by 2029-05-18.
5) Soojin to consolidate final materials and schedule Security signoff (target 2029-05-20).

I've attached the interim artifacts to the drive link and left inline comments in the spreadsheet. Please add estimated effort for each action to the JIRA ticket INFRA-1428.

Thanks all — good momentum.

Soojin
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
